Senses.Explanation: Meeting no one who knows the sound: the ferry-woman's drowning line, the emperor's missed exchange, and the halls' maxims on the unhearable — turned by Yunsou into a mother's refusal and priced by Konggu at half a copper coin. Zhenjing Kewen, in the record's raising-the-old-case section: Yantou Quanhuo, after the purge, worked a ferry on the lake; a woman came holding a child and asked — the oar-dance set aside, where did the child in your arms come from? — he struck her, and she said: I bore seven sons, met no one who knew the sound, and this last one too is not needed — and threw him into the water; the master's crack: the despiser of the enemy perishes. Hansong Zhicao, in his raising-and-verse series: Yunmen Wenyan, asked what a buddha is, answered a dried dung pellet — this one pellet has thrown doubt on no few under heaven; a true dragon-devouring garuda has its own sky-splitting swiftness, but the dung-rolling beetle never thinks of leaving the ground — and his verse: the cuckoo sings in the night still and wind clear, each cry within the old misty vines; were there not boundless heartbreak, the regret at meeting no one who knows the sound would not run so deep. Konggu Daocheng, opening the winter binding at the Myriad-Buddha cloister: seize the patriarch's tally and every staff draws blood; hold up the beam of the teaching and every word cuts the trail — scouring out our right-and-wrong there is another stretch of news: meet no one who knows the sound, do not speak it; speak it, and it is not worth half a copper coin — what is it? Half a catty makes eight ounces, two fives make ten. Yongjue Yuanxian, retelling the Guishan story: the monk who had sold his cloth and traveled three thousand li for the laugh heard that Mingzhao Qian had come forth and went straight to bow; asked what Guishan had said, he raised it, and Zhao ruled: Guishan was head straight and tail straight, only he met no one who knew the sound; asked where the words go when the tree falls and the vine dries — that makes Guishan's laugh turn new — and at those words he woke: the laugh had a knife in it; he bowed toward the far mountain and repented. Tianyin Yuanxiu, raising the same ferry case: a woman came with a child in her arms — the oar-dance set aside, where did the child come from? — the master struck, she answered with the drowning line, and his verse: seven sons all thrown to the green waves, the more you puzzle the more it tangles; folk follow their eyes on the clear stream and see only the mother pitying the child, never the old woman. Fushi Tongxian, putting the line to the assembly: the woman bore seven sons, six met no one who knew the sound, and this last one too was not needed, thrown down into the water — having met the one who knows the sound, why is even this one not needed? They could not answer, and he answered himself: the single word knowing is the gate of a hundred calamities. Baichi Xingyuan, at the year-end minor assembly: one firecracker and heaven and earth shake — where will the sprites stick out their heads? He thought on old Wang burning paper, too timid, laughed at Beichan getting dragged into dividing the year — the mountain does not wrong the worthies of old, only the gate-wind differs — is there anyone among you who can deliver? No one answered, and the master ruled: with no guest who knows the sound, talking of the year's cold is labor in vain — and he dragged his staff and broke up the sitting. Yunsou Benzhu, asked the point of the same line, answers in the mother's voice: I only got you, this one son; true, you met no one who knows the sound — but how could I throw you into the water?
